title: Add resumable partial-response RAG quickstart and compact prober
author: Ava Martinez
merge_commit_message:
feat(quickstart): resumable partial-response RAG quickstart + compact prober

Adds an authoring and runtime example that demonstrates how to resume interrupted streaming generation and incremental retrieval in RAG flows. Includes smoke prober for CI to validate resume semantics and lightweight telemetry presets.
description:
Motivation: production RAG flows deployed in constrained networks (mobile, edge, flaky VPNs) can experience interrupted streaming responses or partial retrievals from index backends. Existing quickstarts show streaming and replay, but consumers repeatedly ask for a minimal, portable pattern to resume mid-response without re-generating large prefixes or losing prior retrieval state. This PR introduces a compact quickstart that demonstrates: 1) how to emit continuation tokens for partial streaming responses; 2) how to checkpoint and replay KV-cache and retrieval cursor state; 3) a small prober that validates resume correctness in CI.

What this change contains: - new quickstart folder "resumable-rag" with a README, demo app (Node/TS), and a tiny server shim that simulates network interruptions; - example instrumentation for Telemetry Presets (span + resume markers) so teams can see resumed vs fresh generations in traces; - a compact prober CLI (python) that runs deterministic smoke tests against the quickstart and asserts end-to-end idempotence after resume; - docs site snippet updates (quickstarts index) and a short how-to in the authoring guide that explains resume trade-offs.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc: ENG-1428 (linked) - [x] Quickstart implementation (Node TS demo + server shim) - [x] Compact prober and CI job snippet - [x] Telemetry presets and example traces - [x] Docs updates and links in quickstarts index - [x] Unit and e2e smoke tests run locally

Notes on design and constraints: - Continuation tokens are application-level opaque strings emitted by the runtime; they include a resume cursor pointer and a short integrity HMAC. The quickstart demonstrates generating them from the client side and validating on resume. - To avoid double-charge risk we recommend the server-side runtime include a resume TTL and idempotency guard; the example includes a minimal in-memory guard that demonstrates the pattern. - Retrieval state is checkpointed as a compact cursor (document ids + vector cursor position) rather than full embedding caches; the demo explains why this is the right cost/latency tradeoff for common mobile flows. - This quickstart intentionally avoids changes to core runtime; the patterns are implemented in the client shim and in retrieval adapters so customers can adopt without runtime upgrades.

How to try it locally (summary): 1) cd quickstarts/resumable-rag 2) npm ci && pip install -r prober/requirements.txt 3) npm run dev to start the shim server (it simulates intermittent TCP resets by default) 4) npm run demo:resume to run the demo client that requests a generation, gets interrupted, then resumes using the continuation token 5) prober/run_smoke.py --target http://localhost:3000 will perform 10 randomized resume attempts and assert token integrity and idempotence

Logging & telemetry: the demo emits OpenTelemetry spans named "resume.attempt" and "generation.continued" with attributes: resume.true, continuation.token.age_ms, retrieval.cursor.count. The quickstart includes a sample Jaeger/OTLP config for local debugging.

Related work & references: - ENG-1428 design notes (linked) - PM-464 product ask for an "offline-friendly RAG UX" - SUP-9981 support case where a customer lost progress on mobile generation after network blips

CI considerations: - The CI job added is intentionally lightweight: it spins up the shim server in Docker (no GPUs), runs the prober, and validates JSON diffs between resumed vs fresh outputs (acceptable differences are configurable via a tolerance flag). - Flaky network simulation runs are limited to smoke stage to keep total CI time stable.

Rollout plan: - Merge to main behind the quickstarts docs banner - Monitor telemetry from the example via an opt-in telemetry collector (only local by default) - Iterate on feedback; suggested follow-ups: a Go example and a dedicated article on idempotency and billing semantics.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Can we make the continuation token format explicit in the README? Also suggested adding a short note about billing idempotency—good to highlight client vs server responsibilities.
Ava Martinez: Added a 'token-format' section to the README and a follow-up note on billing semantics. Kept server-side guard example intentionally minimal with comments on production knobs.
Priya Nair: Telemetry attrs look good. Please add an example trace screenshot or link to records so teams know what to look for.
Ava Martinez: Uploaded a sample Jaeger trace file under telemetry/trace_samples and referenced it in the README.
Marco Giannini: CI smoke job looks fine but increase retries to 3 for network fuzz to reduce flakiness.
Ava Martinez: Increased retries and added a fast-fail flag for local runs. Reran CI locally and pushed a fix for a race condition in the in-memory guard.
release_notes: Introduce a resumable RAG quickstart that demonstrates continuation tokens, client-side resume logic, and a compact CI prober to validate idempotent resumes. No runtime changes. Useful for mobile/edge/offline-first scenarios.
notes_for_maintainers: This quickstart intentionally keeps runtime surface unchanged; it lives in quickstarts/resumable-rag. If we later add it to the docs site nav, ensure the quickstarts index entry points to the README anchor 'resume-flow'. The CI workflow added is opt-in and gated by a resume-smoke label—we won't run it on every PR by default.
changelog_entry: quickstarts: add resumable partial-response RAG quickstart + compact prober (ENG-1428)
audits_or_security: No sensitive data included. The prober uses deterministic inputs and local-only telemetry. Continuation tokens in examples are HMAC-based but use a demo secret stored in environment variables; docs warn to replace with KMS/HSM in production.
testing_instructions: See README in quickstarts/resumable-rag. The prober supports --ci and --local flags; run with --local for iterative debugging. The server shim exposes a /fuzz endpoint to toggle network reset frequency.
post_merge_actions: - Monitor quickstart telemetry for adoption signals - Draft a short blog post and include a banner in next release notes - Consider adding an official Go example if adoption metrics justify it
